title: Afflicted by a Gracious God
description: Afflicted by a Gracious God in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 331.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-fflic-ted by a gra-cious God, The stroke I pa-tient-ly sus-tain, Griev-ous to fee-ble flesh and blood; Un-a-ble to re-joice in pain, Be-neath my Fa-ther's hand I bow, And groan to feel his chas-tening now.

lines: Grievous to feeble flesh and blood;
Beneath my Father's hand I bow,
And groan to feel his chastening now.
But when he hath my patience proved,
And sees me to his will resigned,
His heavy hand and rod removed
Shall leave the blest effect behind,
With which my soul and flesh are filled,
The pure and perfect love shall yield;
The work and praise are all his own.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
